header.title: Crisis severity
header.lead: INFORM Risk shows where a crisis would hit hardest before it happens. INFORM Severity measures how serious an unfolding crisis is: its impact, the conditions of the people affected and the complexity of the response.
header.riskSub: Before a crisis · 0–10 · open the risk explorer

illustrativeNote: They use plausible magnitudes to demonstrate the method. Replace every figure with assessed data before using a result in a situation report.

scenario.title: Start from a scenario
scenario.lead: Load an illustrative Tanzanian crisis to see the method at work, or start a blank assessment.

area.title: Define the affected area
area.lead: Click councils on the map, or pick them from the list. Their 2022 census population and area can then fill the Impact inputs.

impact.lead: How big is the crisis? The size of the affected area and the people living there (geographical, ⅓), and the people affected, displaced or killed (human, ⅔).

conditions.lead: How bad are the conditions of the people affected? Estimate how many people are at each level of humanitarian conditions.

complexity.lead: How hard is it to respond? The structural context (society and safety) and the operating environment on the ground.

reliability.title: Reliability
reliability.lead: How far can the result be trusted? Reported next to the index, never mixed into it.

landslide.name: Landslide

sub.geographicalLead: The scale of the crisis in space and population.
sub.humanLead: Direct effects on people. The percentages are derived automatically.
sub.conditionsLead: Place everyone in the affected area on the five levels of humanitarian conditions (INFORM Severity, Table 1). People at levels 3–5 are the people in need; level 1 is filled in automatically as the remainder.
sub.societySafetyLead: National structural indicators for Tanzania, pre-filled from public sources. Edit them if local evidence for the affected area differs.
sub.operatingEnvironmentLead: Who is affected, and how hard it is for aid and people to reach each other.

areaAffectedKm2.label: Area affected
areaAffectedKm2.help: Land area inside the affected zone. Tip: fill it from the councils selected in step 2.

peopleInArea.label: People living in the affected area
peopleInArea.help: Everyone living in the affected area, affected or not (for example the 2022 census).

peopleAffected.label: People affected
peopleAffected.help: People whose lives, homes or livelihoods were directly hit.

displaced.label: People displaced
displaced.help: People forced from their homes: in camps, public buildings or with host families.

fatalities.label: Fatalities
fatalities.help: Deaths caused by the event, including missing people presumed dead.

groups.label: Population groups affected
groups.help: Tick every group the crisis affects. The more diverse the groups, the more complex the response.

accessOfActors.label: Access of relief actors to people
accessOfActors.help: Restricted movement, bureaucratic hurdles, interference or violence against aid workers.

accessOfPeople.label: Access of people to assistance
accessOfPeople.help: People unable to reach services or aid, or restricted in their movement.

physicalSecurityConstraints.label: Physical and security constraints
physicalSecurityConstraints.help: Washed-out roads and bridges, flood water, difficult terrain or insecurity.

gini.label: Income inequality (Gini index)
gini.help: 0 = perfect equality, 100 = maximal inequality. Higher inequality weakens social cohesion.

genderInequality.label: Gender Inequality Index (UNDP)
genderInequality.help: 0 = equality between women and men, 1 = maximal inequality.

conflictIntensity.label: Conflict intensity
conflictIntensity.help: 0 = no conflict … 5 = war (HIIK Conflict Barometer scale), for the affected area.

violenceFatalities.label: Fatalities from political violence
violenceFatalities.help: Deaths from organised violence in the last 12 months (for example ACLED).

corruptionPerception.label: Corruption Perceptions Index
corruptionPerception.help: 0 = highly corrupt, 100 = very clean. Higher is better, so the score is inverted.

ruleOfLawPercentile.label: Rule of law (WGI percentile)
ruleOfLawPercentile.help: Percentile rank among countries. Higher is better, so the score is inverted.

daysSinceUpdate.label: Days since the data were last updated
daysSinceUpdate.help: Updates within 30 days score highest; data older than a year score lowest.

derived.affectedPct: {{v}}% of the people in the area

5.name: Extreme
5.desc: Widespread loss of life or irreversible harm. Living standards have collapsed and coping options are exhausted.

4.name: Severe
4.desc: Living standards have broken down. Survival depends on humanitarian aid or emergency coping; serious physical and mental harm.

3.name: Moderate
3.desc: Living standards are degrading. Some basic needs cannot be met without crisis coping, such as selling productive assets.

2.name: Stressed
2.desc: Living standards are under stress. Basic needs are met only through coping that erodes livelihoods.

1.name: None or minimal
1.desc: Acceptable living standards; basic needs are met without harmful coping. Calculated as the rest of the people in the area.

conditions.distribution: People in the area by level of conditions
conditions.needArea: Enter the people living in the affected area (step 3) to see the distribution and the concentration of conditions.
conditions.concentrationSub: Highest level whose cumulative share, counted from level 5 down, exceeds 5% of the people in the area

source.conflictIntensity: HIIK Conflict Barometer scale 0–5 · analyst judgement
source.ruleOfLawPercentile: World Bank · WGI Rule of Law percentile

access.notSet: Not assessed yet. Pick a score from 0 (no constraints) to 3 (high constraints).

0.name: None
0.desc: No access constraints: aid and people move freely.

1.name: Low
1.desc: Occasional restrictions or delays; most people can be reached.

2.name: Moderate
2.desc: Regular restrictions; parts of the area or population are hard to reach.

3.name: High
3.desc: Severe restrictions; large parts of the affected population cannot be reached.

low.name: Low
low.desc: Unverified reports, a single source or rough estimates.

medium.name: Medium
medium.desc: Partial assessments or preliminary official figures.

high.name: High
high.desc: Verified multi-sector assessment or official statistics.

reliabilityNote: The reliability index combines source reliability, recency and data completeness. It is shown next to the severity score and never changes it.

table.title: From raw figures to 0–5 scores
table.lead: Each indicator is scaled between a reference minimum and maximum. Counts of people use a log scale, so going from 1,000 to 10,000 people weighs as much as going from 10,000 to 100,000.
table.caption: Severity indicators with raw values, calibration parameters and 0–5 scores
table.calibrationHint: Reference ranges calibrated for sub-national crises in Tanzania. They are model parameters, not observed data.

derivation.peopleInAreaPct: People in the area ÷ Tanzania’s population ({{pop}}, 2022 census) × 100
derivation.peopleAffectedPct: People affected ÷ people in the area × 100
derivation.peopleInNeed: Sum of the people at levels 3, 4 and 5
derivation.concentrationLevel: Highest level whose cumulative share (from level 5 down) exceeds 5% of the people in the area
derivation.groupsAffected: Number of distinct population groups affected (maximum 5)

method.title: How the INFORM Severity Index is built
method.lead: Indicators are scaled to 0–5, averaged into components, combined into categories and dimensions with INFORM’s geometric mean, and weighted into one index.
method.legendG: INFORM weighted geometric mean (inverted, so high values dominate)
method.live: Scores in the boxes update live with your inputs.

normalise.title: Scale every indicator
normalise.body: Each indicator is mapped to 0–5 between a reference minimum and maximum. Absolute counts use log₁₀(1 + x) so that orders of magnitude count equally; indicators where higher is better are inverted.

aggregate.title: Aggregate
aggregate.body: Indicators are averaged into components. Components, categories and dimensions are combined with G, INFORM’s weighted geometric mean, so one very severe aspect is not diluted by milder ones.

classify.title: Classify
classify.body: Severity = 0.7 × G(Impact ⅓, Conditions ⅔) + 0.3 × Complexity, reported with one decimal. The category is the score rounded up: 3.1 is category 4 (High), 3.0 is category 3 (Medium).

reliability.title: Qualify
reliability.body: Source reliability, recency and completeness form a separate 1–5 reliability index. It tells you how far to trust the result but never changes it.

method.adapt: The structure, weights, geometric aggregation and round-up categories follow the official method. The indicator reference ranges are calibration parameters for sub-national Tanzanian crises; the Society & safety defaults are national structural indicators.
method.denominators: National denominators: {{pop}} people (NBS 2022 census) and {{area}} km².
